proposals.before: Li Kui, whose courtesy name was Duanching, came from Longxi Chenji but his family had long lived in Zhengzhou, where for generations they ranked among the foremost great houses.
proposals.after: Li Kui, whose courtesy name was Duanqing, came from Longxi Chengji but his family had long lived in Zhengzhou, where for generations they ranked among the foremost great houses.
proposals.reason: 端卿 romanizes as Duanqing, not Duanching; 成紀 is Chengji, not Chenji.

proposals.before: Li Kui, styled Duanching, was a native of Longxi Chenji but his family resided in Zhengzhou; for generations they were a leading clan.
proposals.after: Li Kui, styled Duanqing, was a native of Longxi Chengji but his family resided in Zhengzhou; for generations they were a leading clan.
proposals.reason: 端卿 romanizes as Duanqing, not Duanching; 成紀 is Chengji, not Chenji.

proposals.before: He was descended from Xuandao, who had served as a scholar in the Prince of Qin's household and as a superviser-remonstrator, and was the son of Chengyu, Director of the Secretariat, who was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.
proposals.after: He was the great-great-grandson of Xuandao, who had served as a scholar in the Prince of Qin's household and as a supervising remonstrator, and was the son of Chengyu, Director of the Secretariat, who was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.
proposals.reason: 玄孫 is great-great-grandson; 給事中 is supervising remonstrator, and superviser is misspelled.

proposals.before: He was the great-grandson of Xuandao, a scholar of the Prince of Qin's household and a superviser-remonstrator; and the son of Chengyu, Director of the Secretariat and posthumously Minister of Personnel.
proposals.after: He was the great-great-grandson of Xuandao, a scholar of the Prince of Qin's household and a supervising remonstrator; and the son of Chengyu, Director of the Secretariat and posthumously Minister of Personnel.
proposals.reason: 玄孫 means great-great-grandson, not great-grandson; superviser is misspelled.

proposals.before: He was then made Right Supplementation-reminder and Attendant of the Heir Apparent, with responsibility for memorials from members of the imperial clan.
proposals.after: He was then made Right Supplementation-reminder and Imperial Diarist, with responsibility for memorials from members of the imperial clan.
proposals.reason: 起居郎 is the Imperial Diarist office, not an attendant of the Heir Apparent.

proposals.before: He was transferred to Right Supplementation-reminder and Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and was charged with imperial-clan memorials.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Right Supplementation-reminder and Imperial Diarist, and was charged with imperial-clan memorials.
proposals.reason: 起居郎 is the Imperial Diarist office, not Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

proposals.before: He rose to outer office director in the Ministry of Personnel and bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, serving in both offices as a drafter of imperial rescripts.
proposals.after: He rose to outer office director of the Bureau of Merits and bureau director of Evaluations in the Ministry of Personnel, serving in both offices as a drafter of imperial rescripts.
proposals.reason: 考功郎中 belongs to the Ministry of Personnel, not Rites; 司勛 is the Bureau of Merits.

proposals.before: He was promoted to outer office director in the Ministry of Personnel and bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, and in both posts drafted imperial rescripts.
proposals.after: He was promoted to outer office director of the Bureau of Merits and bureau director of Evaluations in the Ministry of Personnel, and in both posts drafted imperial rescripts.
proposals.reason: 考功郎中 is a Ministry of Personnel post, not Ministry of Rites.

proposals.before: His colleague Lü Yin, though far beneath him in birth and standing, had once outranked him in government. After leaving the chief ministership Lü went from imperial guest to military commissioner of Jingnan, where his reputation flourished.
proposals.after: His colleague Lü Yin, though far beneath him in birth and standing, surpassed him in handling of government affairs. After leaving the chief ministership Lü went from imperial guest to military commissioner of Jingnan, where his reputation flourished.
proposals.reason: 政事在揆之右 means Lü's governance was superior to Kui's, not that Lü had outranked him in office.

proposals.before: Yin submitted a secret memorial in his own defense, and Kui was demoted to senior administrator of Laizhou. The edict declared, "He stirred up the eight prefectures south of the lake and obstructed control from Jiangling."
proposals.after: Yin submitted a secret memorial in his own defense, and Kui was demoted to senior administrator of Laizhou with concurrent regular status. The edict declared, "He stirred up the eight prefectures south of the lake and obstructed control from Jiangling."
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 同正員 (concurrent regular status), which the Chinese and literal both preserve.

proposals.before: Soon someone said: "When Han was formerly Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court he said nothing; now as Junior Tutor he presumptuously submitted this opinion."
proposals.after: Soon someone said: "When Han was formerly Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court he said nothing; now as Junior Tutor, his aide presumptuously submitted this opinion."
proposals.reason: Chinese 妄有奏議 refers to the aide's memorial on Han's behalf; the idiomatic correctly attributes it to the aide while the literal wrongly makes Han the submitter.

proposals.before: In the Zhide era Wang Silu, military commissioner of Hedong, recommended him as staff adviser. He rose through appointments as rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, investigating palace censor, and military commissioner aide.
proposals.after: In the Zhide era Wang Sili, military commissioner of Hedong, recommended him as staff adviser. He rose through appointments as rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, investigating palace censor, and military commissioner aide.
proposals.reason: 王思禮 is standardly Wang Sili (Sīlǐ); Silu misreads 禮.

proposals.before: In the Zhide era Wang Silu, military commissioner of Hedong, memorialized that he be made staff adviser; he was repeatedly appointed rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, investigating palace censor, and military commissioner aide.
proposals.after: In the Zhide era Wang Sili, military commissioner of Hedong, memorialized that he be made staff adviser; he was repeatedly appointed rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, investigating palace censor, and military commissioner aide.
proposals.reason: 王思禮 is standardly Wang Sili (Sīlǐ); Silu misreads 禮.

proposals.before: In the second year of Yongtai Baoyu again recommended him as marching army vice marshal of Longyou and acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, while retaining his concurrent post as Censor-in-chief.
proposals.after: In the second year of Yongtai, Baoyu again recommended him as marching army vice marshal of Longyou and acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, while retaining his concurrent post as Censor-in-chief.
proposals.reason: Missing comma after Yongtai fuses the reign name with Baoyu into a false personal name.

proposals.before: In the second year of Yongtai Baoyu again memorialized that he be made marching army vice marshal of Longyou, appointed acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and as before concurrently Censor-in-chief.
proposals.after: In the second year of Yongtai, Baoyu again memorialized that he be made marching army vice marshal of Longyou, appointed acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and as before concurrently Censor-in-chief.
proposals.reason: Missing comma after Yongtai fuses the reign name with Baoyu into a false personal name.

proposals.before: When Dezong took the throne, Shaoyou was repeatedly given acting appointments as Minister of Rites and Minister of War.
proposals.after: When the emperor took the throne, he was repeatedly given acting appointments as Minister of Rites and Minister of War.
proposals.reason: Chinese 上即位 does not name Dezong; the idiomatic line invents the temple name and also inserts Shaoyou where the Chinese subject is silent.

proposals.before: Before long Liu Qia recovered Bianzhou and obtained Xilie's false attendance diary, which recorded that on a certain day Chen Shaoyou had submitted a memorial of submission."
proposals.after: Before long Liu Qia recovered Bianzhou and obtained Xilie's false attendance diary, which recorded: "On a certain day Chen Shaoyou submitted a memorial of submission."
proposals.reason: The original English retained only a closing quote. The revised sentence restores the explicitly quoted diary entry in the Chinese.

proposals.before: When Shaoyou's envoy arrived in succession, the emperor asked: "Did Shaoyou take Bao Ji's funds and goods?"
proposals.after: When Shaoyou's envoy then arrived, the emperor asked: "Did Shaoyou take Bao Ji's funds and goods?"
proposals.reason: 繼至 means the envoy arrived afterward/next, not that multiple envoys arrived "in succession."

proposals.before: Lu Qi hated him and prompted the relevant offices to impeach him. He was demoted to vice prefect of Fuzhou, then reassigned as prefect of Raozhou, and later transferred to prefect of Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian.
proposals.after: Lu Qi hated him and prompted the relevant offices to impeach him. He was demoted to vice prefect of Fu Prefecture, then reassigned as prefect of Raozhou, and later transferred to prefect of Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian.
proposals.reason: Chinese 撫州 (Fu Prefecture) is distinct from later 福州 (Fuzhou); rendering both as Fuzhou collapses two places.

proposals.before: Lu Qi greatly hated him, hinted that the relevant offices impeach him, and he was demoted to vice prefect of Fuzhou with concurrent regular status, then changed to prefect of Raozhou and transferred to prefect of Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian.
proposals.after: Lu Qi greatly hated him, hinted that the relevant offices impeach him, and he was demoted to vice prefect of Fu Prefecture with concurrent regular status, then changed to prefect of Raozhou and transferred to prefect of Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian.
proposals.reason: Chinese 撫州 must be distinguished from 福州; both were wrongly rendered as Fuzhou.

proposals.before: Before long the Prince of Guo recommended him as attendant censor and agricultural colony aide of Xiang and Deng. He then entered mourning for his mother.
proposals.after: Before long the Prince of Guo, Ju, recommended him as attendant censor and agricultural colony aide of Xiang and Deng. He then entered mourning for his mother.
proposals.reason: Chinese 虢王巨 names the prince as Ju; the idiomatic English omits that personal name.

proposals.before: After the rebels were pacified he was appointed Palace Companion of the Heir Apparent and promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites. He was repeatedly summoned to speak on affairs of state.
proposals.after: After the rebels were pacified he was appointed Palace Companion of the Heir Apparent and promoted to bureau director for merit evaluation. He was repeatedly summoned to speak on affairs of state.
proposals.reason: 考功郎中 belongs to the Personnel merit-evaluation bureau, not the Ministry of Rites.

proposals.before: When the rebels were pacified he was appointed Palace Companion of the Heir Apparent, promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, and repeatedly summoned to speak on affairs.
proposals.after: When the rebels were pacified he was appointed Palace Companion of the Heir Apparent, promoted to bureau director for merit evaluation, and repeatedly summoned to speak on affairs.
proposals.reason: 考功郎中 is not an office of the Ministry of Rites.

proposals.before: When Daizong was in Shan, Xu walked to the mobile court carrying the seals of the Ministry of Rites and the Southern Bureau. The emperor saw him and said, "The fierce wind reveals the tough grass—how true that saying is."
proposals.after: When Daizong was in Shan, Xu walked to the mobile court carrying the seals of the merit-evaluation bureau and the Southern Bureau. The emperor saw him and said, "The fierce wind reveals the tough grass—how true that saying is."
proposals.reason: 考功及南曹 are Personnel ministry seals, not Ministry of Rites seals.

proposals.before: When Daizong was in Shan, Xu walked carrying the seals of the Ministry of Rites and the Southern Bureau to the mobile court; the emperor saw him and said: "The fierce wind reveals the tough grass—how true indeed."
proposals.after: When Daizong was in Shan, Xu walked carrying the seals of the merit-evaluation bureau and the Southern Bureau to the mobile court; the emperor saw him and said: "The fierce wind reveals the tough grass—how true indeed."
proposals.reason: 考功及南曹 are not Ministry of Rites seals.

proposals.before: The Meritous Father, Prince of Fenyang Guo Ziyi, had a servant kill a sheep and bring it in. The gate guards detected it, and Xu submitted a detailed memorial. The emperor thought he did not fear the powerful and repeatedly sent imperial commendation.
proposals.after: The Meritorious Father, Prince of Fenyang Guo Ziyi, had a servant kill a sheep and bring it in. The gate guards detected it, and Xu submitted a detailed memorial. The emperor thought he did not fear the powerful and repeatedly sent imperial commendation.
proposals.reason: 尚父 is Meritorious Father; Meritous is a clear English misspelling.

proposals.before: The Meritous Father, Prince of Fenyang Guo Ziyi, had a servant kill a sheep and bring it in; the gate guards detected it, and Xu submitted a detailed memorial; the emperor thought he did not fear the powerful and repeatedly sent imperial commendation.
proposals.after: The Meritorious Father, Prince of Fenyang Guo Ziyi, had a servant kill a sheep and bring it in; the gate guards detected it, and Xu submitted a detailed memorial; the emperor thought he did not fear the powerful and repeatedly sent imperial commendation.
proposals.reason: 尚父 should be Meritorious Father, not Meritous Father.

proposals.before: Shaoyou chased profit and power as the times shifted; Lu Qi cultivated the powerful and favored as a crafty office-seeker—in examining their words and conduct, none is praiseworthy.
proposals.after: Shaoyou chased profit and power as the times shifted; Lu Ji cultivated the powerful and favored as a crafty office-seeker—in examining their words and conduct, none is praiseworthy.
proposals.reason: Chinese 盧惎 is Lu Ji (惎), not Lu Qi; the idiomatic English mistranslates the given name.

proposals.before: Shaoyou chased profit and power as times shifted; Lu Qi served the powerful and favored as a crafty office-seeker—in examining words and observing conduct, none is praiseworthy.
proposals.after: Shaoyou chased profit and power as times shifted; Lu Ji served the powerful and favored as a crafty office-seeker—in examining words and observing conduct, none is praiseworthy.
proposals.reason: Chinese 盧惎 is Lu Ji (惎), not Lu Qi; the literal English mistranslates the given name.

proposals.before: The eulogy says: Li, Chen, and Lu Bie—their words and conduct were not genuine.
proposals.after: The eulogy says: Li, Chen, and Lu Yue—their words and conduct were not genuine.
proposals.reason: Chinese 盧鸑 is Lu Yue (鸑), not Lu Bie; the idiomatic English romanization is wrong.

proposals.before: The eulogy says: Li, Chen, and Lu Bie—their words and conduct were not genuine.
proposals.after: The eulogy says: Li, Chen, and Lu Yue—their words and conduct were not genuine.
proposals.reason: Chinese 盧鸑 is Lu Yue (鸑), not Lu Bie; the literal English romanization is wrong.

decisions.reason: s0001 字端卿 and 隴西成紀 require courtesy-name Duanqing and place Chengji; Duanching and Chenji are romanization errors.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 李揆字端卿，隴西成紀人

decisions.reason: The literal field repeats the same 端卿→Duanching and 成紀→Chenji errors; Duanqing and Chengji are correct.
s0002 玄孫 is the fourth-generation descendant (great-great-grandson), not a vague 'descended from'; 給事中 is supervising remonstrator, and 'superviser' is misspelled.
Literal 'great-grandson' understates 玄孫; great-great-grandson is the correct kinship term, and supervising remonstrator fixes the office spelling.
s0005 起居郎 is the Imperial Diarist office, not Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
The literal likewise misrenders 起居郎 as Attendant of the Heir Apparent; Imperial Diarist matches the Chinese office.
s0006 司勛員外郎 and 考功郎中 are both Personnel posts (Bureau of Merits; Evaluations); assigning 考功 to the Ministry of Rites is wrong.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遷司勛員外郎、考功郎中

decisions.reason: Literal repeats the Ministry of Rites error for 考功郎中; both offices belong under the Ministry of Personnel.

decisions.after: His colleague Lü Yin, though far beneath him in birth and standing, surpassed him in government affairs. After leaving the chief ministership Lü went from imperial guest to military commissioner of Jingnan, where his reputation flourished.
decisions.reason: s0034 政事在揆之右 means Lü's governance was superior to Kui's, not that he had outranked him in office; the proposal's sense is right, but 'in handling of government affairs' is awkward, so the phrasing is tightened.
s0036 萊州長史同正員 includes concurrent regular status; idiomatic English wrongly drops 同正員.
s0068 妄有奏議, clarified by s0069 呂渭僭陳章奏…為其本使, attributes the presumptuous memorial to Han's aide, not to Han himself; the literal wrongly makes Han the submitter.
s0086 王思禮 romanizes as Wang Sili (禮 lǐ); Silu misreads the given name.
Literal repeats Wang Silu for 王思禮; Wang Sili is the correct romanization.
s0094 永泰二年，抱玉 again separates the reign date from the person Baoyu; without the comma, 'Yongtai Baoyu' reads as a false compound name.
The literal has the same missing comma after Yongtai that fuses the date with Baoyu.

The surrounding biography explicitly identifies both Dezong and Shaoyou, so the existing idiomatic sentence resolves two otherwise ambiguous pronouns without changing the Chinese meaning. The proposal would make the prose harder to follow.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 上即位，累加檢校禮部、兵部尚書

decisions.reason: The repair should restore the complete quoted diary entry rather than merely deleting its unmatched closing quotation mark.
s0141 會少遊使繼至 means the envoy then/next arrived after Bao Ji's pellet memorial, not that multiple envoys arrived 'in succession'.
s0162 distinguishes 撫州 from later 福州; rendering the demotion post as Fuzhou collapses two different places.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 坐貶撫州司馬同正…遷福州刺史

decisions.reason: Literal likewise renders 撫州 as Fuzhou; Fu Prefecture correctly separates it from 福州.
s0169 虢王巨 names the prince Ju; idiomatic English omits that personal name while the literal preserves it.
s0175 考功郎中 is the Personnel merit-evaluation bureau director, not an office of the Ministry of Rites.
Literal repeats the Ministry of Rites misassignment for 考功郎中; bureau director for merit evaluation is correct.
s0176 考功及南曹二印 are the merit-evaluation and Southern Bureau seals of Personnel, not Ministry of Rites seals.
Literal likewise mislabels 考功 as Ministry of Rites; merit-evaluation bureau is the correct referent.
s0192 尚父 is Meritorious Father; 'Meritous' is a misspelling in the idiomatic English.
Literal repeats the misspelling Meritous for 尚父; Meritorious Father is the correct English title.
s0211 盧惎 is Lu Ji; Lu Qi misreads 惎 as if it were 杞.
Literal likewise mistranslates 盧惎 as Lu Qi; Lu Ji matches the Chinese given name.
s0213 盧鸑 romanizes as Lu Yue; Bie is an incorrect reading of 鸑.
Literal repeats Lu Bie for 盧鸑; Lu Yue is the correct romanization.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows English Duanching was only a mistranslation of 端卿; the courtesy-name claim must read Duanqing.
Accepted r0012 shows English Silu was only a mistranslation of 思禮; the personal-name claim must read Wang Sili.
Accepted r0012 likewise requires the given-name claim to read Sili rather than Silu.
Accepted r0026 corrects the misspelled English title Meritous Father to Meritorious Father for 尚父.
Accepted r0026 likewise requires the honor claim label to read Meritorious Father.
